### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. colorectal cancer  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5467340, Reactome:R-HSA-5467348, Reactome:R-HSA-5689896, Reactome:R-HSA-5339716, Reactome:R-HSA-5358747)

**Proposed mechanism:** APC (HGNC:583) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (R-HSA-9019856); CTNNB1 (HGNC:2514) —INCREASES→ Wnt signaling pathway (R-HSA-9019856); Wnt signaling pathway (R-HSA-9019856) —LEADS_TO→ Cell cycle regulation (R-HSA-9019856); TP53 (HGNC:11998) —DISRUPTS→ Cell cycle regulation (R-HSA-9019856); Cell cycle regulation (R-HSA-9019856) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatocellular carcinoma (MONDO:0007256); Cell cycle regulation (R-HSA-9019856) —LEADS_TO→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575). Mutations in APC lead to the destabilization of the destruction complex, allowing CTNNB1 to accumulate and activate the Wnt signaling pathway. Simultaneously, TP53 mutations disrupt cell cycle regulation. Both dysregulated Wnt signaling and impaired cell cycle control converge to promote uncontrolled cell proliferation, leading to both hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of distinct, non-overlapping sets of core causal genes and pathways uniquely associated with each disease, with no significant overlap in mutation profiles of key regulators like APC, CTNNB1, and TP53, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Presence of common benign variants (e.g., gnomAD allele frequency > 1%) in the critical regulatory regions of APC, CTNNB1, or TP53 that are implicated in both diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting common pathways such as Wnt signaling or cell cycle checkpoints could lead to the development of broad-spectrum anti-cancer therapies effective against both hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer, or inform personalized treatment strategies based on shared molecular vulnerabilities.

**Why it matters:** Targeting aberrant Wnt signaling or cell cycle regulators could offer therapeutic strategies for both hepatocellular carcinoma and gastric adenocarcinoma and proximal polyposis of the stomach.
